title: PRD: Staged degradation playbook for gateway throttles and autoscale stalls
creator: Marco Reyes
description:
Summary:
After the 2025-02-10 regional gateway incident (INC-2025-02-10-GW), autoscaler lag and a delayed pool creation combined with an aggressive global routing policy to create a sustained gateway throttle affecting Dedicated tenants. This ticket converts the postmortem action items into concrete PRD updates: a staged degradation playbook, testable acceptance criteria, synthetic canaries, and per-tenant fallback budgets. The goal is to ensure repeatable operational response, measurable failure-mode coverage, and automated verification in CI/canary environments.

Background & motivation:
- Incident root causes: autoscaler API timeout on control plane manifests, slow kernel rollouts on a new GPU SKU, and a routing policy that prioritized regional affinity too aggressively.
- Customer impact: 20% request error rate for affected tenants for ~45 minutes, with 3 enterprise customers filing SEV escalations.
- Postmortem ask: Translate the remediation checklist into shipping requirements, add acceptance tests, and define rollback/mitigation gates for releases.

This PRD update will be the source of truth for: rollout gates, observable thresholds that trigger automated fallbacks, runbook automation hooks, and acceptance criteria for engineers and SREs.
decision_notes: Adopt staged degradation vs full failover: reduces blast radius for high-cardinality tenants and aligns with cost/latency tradeoffs.
Implement per-tenant fallback budgets (quota of allowed degraded operations per hour) rather than global circuit breakers to avoid noisy neighbor issues.
Synthetic canaries will run before each major rollout and after autoscaler config changes; canaries must verify both cache rehydration and routing fallback behavior.
progress_updates: 2025-02-21: Draft PRD outline created and shared with SREs (link below). Requested ENG estimations for autoscaler hooks and routing policy feature work.
2025-02-25: SRE feedback incorporated — added metric for failed pool creation time and a new acceptance test for canary traffic shaping.
2025-03-03: Engineering spike approved to prototype automatic fallback trigger on pool-creation latency > 2m; added ENG-72111 as dependency.
acceptance_criteria: Automated canary verifies the following within 10 minutes of run: p95 latency < 1200ms, successful KV cache rehydration on 90% of sample sessions, and successful routing fallback in 99% of simulated pool-loss events.

A staged degradation playbook exists in the repo and runbook system with clear trigger thresholds: pool-creation-latency > 2m, tail-error-rate > 5% for 5m, or sustained CPU > 85% on routing nodes for 3m.
Per-tenant fallback budgets implemented and testable: simulate tenant with quota exhausted and verify fallback to lower-cost model variant within 30s and error budget decrement is recorded.

Release gating: any rollout that modifies autoscaler or routing policy must pass the synthetic canary (green) and have rollback criteria documented; failure to pass blocks merge for the release branch.

Operational automation: runbook steps 1-3 can be triggered via Slackbot / webhook and must complete (or escalate) within defined timers; average time to rollback for a failed canary < 15 minutes in staging.
Observability & alerting: metrics and dashboards added with relevant SLOs and an on-call pager rule; alerts include runbook link and suggested mitigation steps.
scope: Create PRD section describing the staged degradation model and decision tree for automated fallbacks.
Define and implement synthetic canary scenarios for cache rehydration, pool creation, and routing fallback.
Add per-tenant fallback budget schema and telemetry to the metrics pipeline.
Add release gating rules and CI checks that run the synthetic canaries pre-release.
Document runbook automation hooks and Slack/webhook play.
out_of_scope: Rewriting the entire autoscaler: only necessary hooks and observability additions are required for this ticket.
Major changes to billing or quota models outside fallback budgets (separate billing initiative).
On-prem private control plane major redesign — only API-compatible hooks.
risks: Risk that synthetic canaries add flakiness to CI if not well-isolated; mitigation: isolate canary infra and use dedicated test buckets.
Per-tenant budgets may require schema migration and careful rollout to avoid impacting live tenants; mitigation: gradual rollout with tenant opt-in and shadowing for 2 weeks.
Automated rollback actions could increase churn if thresholds are too sensitive; mitigation: staged thresholds and operator-visible dry-run mode.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging, 2 weeks): implement canary scenarios, add dashboards, and validate metrics ingestion.
Phase 2 (canary tenants, 2 weeks): enable per-tenant fallback budgets in shadow mode for 10% of tenants and run controlled chaos during low-traffic windows.
Phase 3 (graduated enable, 4 weeks): enable enforcement on 50% of tenants with operator monitoring and 24/7 SRE on-call overlap, then full roll after OKRs met.
Rollback criteria: failed synthetic canary OR sustained increase in customer errors beyond 1.5x baseline for 15m triggers immediate rollback to previous routing profile.
testing_plan: Unit tests for fallback budget accounting and API validation.
Integration tests covering canary traffic paths: KV cache priming, pool loss simulation, and routing fallback verification.
Chaos test: scheduled pool termination in staging to validate automated fallback and runbook escalation.
Acceptance test in CI: canary must pass with stable metrics for 3 consecutive runs before gating merge.
notes_for_engineering: ENG asks: provide eng-side estimates for autoscaler hook (ENG-72111) and routing policy feature (ENG-73490).
Prefer feature-flagged rollout for fallback budgets with clear telemetry and an operator-visible enable/disable toggle.
Design should avoid adding high-cardinality tags to critical metrics; use tenant hash bucketing for sampling traces.
